iti89:1.1: This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
iti89:2.1: “Monks, conquered by three forms of false Dhamma–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for an eon.
iti89:2.2: Which three? Conquered by evil desires–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for the duration of an eon.
iti89:2.4: Conquered by friendship with evil people–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for the duration of an eon.
iti89:2.5: And, there being something further to be done, he nevertheless stopped halfway with a lower modicum of distinctive attainment.
iti89:2.6: Conquered by these three forms of false Dhamma–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for an eon.”
iti89:3.2: May no one in the world ever be reborn with evil desire.
iti89:3.3: Know that through that evil desire,
iti89:3.4: his destination’s that of all who have evil desires.
iti89:4.4: I’ve heard how Devadatta, –regarded as wise, composed, incandescent with honor–
iti89:5.3: and fell to the four-gated, fearful place: Avīci, unmitigated hell.
iti89:6.3: who’s done no evil deed: that evil touches him himself,
iti89:7.2: of polluting the ocean with a pot of poison,
iti89:7.4: for the mass of water is great.
iti89:8.1: So it is when anyone attacks with abuse
iti89:8.4: for abuse doesn’t grow on him.
iti89:9.1: A wise person should make friends, should associate, with a person like him–
iti89:9.2: whose path a monk can pursue
iti89:9.4: and reach the ending of suffering & stress.
